versions.rationale: Single patch for active model/session construction evidence and a version-pinned API distinction; no prior bump or repeated increments.

changes.finding: The existing guidance collected provider/version support but did not explicitly acquire the actual session factory and arguments serving the request.
changes.change: Trace selected model/session factory and active model generation plus creation options; configuration presence or availability logs alone do not establish the used path.
changes.consequence: Prevents tuning an unused configuration or attributing behavior to a model/session not used by the caller.

changes.finding: The placement section correctly distinguished registration from execution, but did not distinguish available/configured provider from options actually applied to the created session.
changes.change: Added ONNX Runtime Java 1.22.0 default-versus-supplied createSession overload example, environment-level availability limit, and session/generation-correlated evidence; reject ignored-options diagnosis when binding is already correct.
changes.consequence: Produces a discriminating factory check and a no-change branch before concurrency tuning; avoids assuming the corrected wiring proves placement or performance.

changes.change: Added exact OrtEnvironment v1.22.0 source for session construction and provider availability.
changes.consequence: Consequential API statements can be verified at the cited version without adopting a new engine version.

preserved: In-process versus remote serving tradeoffs and preservation of an adequate boundary.
Existing output-contract and model-owner acceptance gates for conversion, batching, precision and provider changes.
Native resource ownership, buffer leases, OrtSession.Result and pinned-output lifetimes, DJL managers/predictors and partial-construction cleanup.
Timeout/cancellation versus actual native completion; generation replacement overlap, admission and drain ownership.

NMT/RSS limits, virtual-thread native execution/pin-event caveats and no universal JDK baseline.
